items.stem: A circuit diagram shows a rectangle with an arrow through it. Which component does this symbol represent?
items.markingKey: A variable resistor is drawn as a rectangle with an arrow through it.

items.stem: A student wants to measure the p.d. across a LED. Explain how the voltmeter should be connected and why.
items.answer: In parallel with the LED, because it measures the energy per coulomb across the component; very high resistance.

items.stem: A student wants to measure the p.d. across a thermistor. Explain how the voltmeter should be connected and why.
items.answer: In parallel with the thermistor, because it measures the energy per coulomb across the component; very high resistance.

items.stem: A circuit diagram shows a cell, switch S1, an ammeter and 2 lamps in series, with a voltmeter across the last lamp. Describe how the readings change when S1 is opened, and explain.
items.answer: Both readings fall to zero: opening the switch breaks the only path, so no current flows and no energy is transferred in the lamp.
items.markingKey: 1 mark both zero; 1 mark single path broken.

items.stem: A circuit diagram shows a cell, switch S1, an ammeter and 3 lamps in series, with a voltmeter across the last lamp. Describe how the readings change when S1 is opened, and explain.
items.answer: Both readings fall to zero: opening the switch breaks the only path, so no current flows and no energy is transferred in the lamp.
items.markingKey: 1 mark both zero; 1 mark single path broken.

items.stem: Zara builds a circuit with a 24 V supply: a 2 Ω resistor, then a junction leading to 4 Ω and 4 Ω resistors in parallel. (a) Calculate the current from the battery. (b) The 4 Ω resistor is removed. State and explain what happens to the battery current.
items.answer: (a) 6.00 A (b) It decreases: total resistance increases (only one path through the parallel section).

items.stem: A circuit diagram shows a small rectangle with a line running through it end to end. Which component does this symbol represent?
items.markingKey: A fuse is drawn as a small rectangle with a line running through it end to end.

items.stem: A student wants to measure the p.d. across a resistor. Explain how the voltmeter should be connected and why.
items.answer: In parallel with the resistor, because it measures the energy per coulomb across the component; very high resistance.

items.stem: Explain why circuit diagrams use standard symbols.
items.answer: Everyone can read them the same way; they are quicker to draw and show connections clearly.

items.stem: A circuit diagram shows a cell, switch S2, an ammeter and 3 lamps in series, with a voltmeter across the last lamp. Describe how the readings change when S2 is opened, and explain.

items.stem: A circuit diagram shows a cell, switch S2, an ammeter and 2 lamps in series, with a voltmeter across the last lamp. Describe how the readings change when S2 is opened, and explain.
items.answer: Both readings fall to zero: opening the switch breaks the only path, so no current flows and no energy is transferred in the lamp.
items.markingKey: 1 mark both zero; 1 mark single path broken.

items.stem: In a circuit, resistor P (5 Ω) is in series with two resistors Q (10 Ω) and R (10 Ω) that are connected in parallel with each other. The supply is 9 V. (a) Calculate the combined resistance of the parallel pair. (b) The 10 Ω resistor is removed. State and explain what happens to the battery current.
items.answer: (a) 5.00 Ω (b) It decreases: total resistance increases (only one path through the parallel section).

items.stem: In a circuit, resistor P (2 Ω) is in series with two resistors Q (3 Ω) and R (6 Ω) that are connected in parallel with each other. The supply is 9 V. (a) Calculate the p.d. across the 2 Ω resistor. (b) Calculate the current in the 3 Ω resistor. (c) Calculate the power dissipated in the whole circuit.
In a parallel circuit, the current from the source is
options: smaller than the current in any branch
equal to the sum of the currents in the branches
zero when a branch is added
items.answer: equal to the sum of the currents in the branches
items.markingKey: Current splits at a junction: I = I₁ + I₂.

items.stem: Explain why lights in a house are wired in parallel.
items.answer: Each lamp gets the full mains p.d.; each can be switched independently; if one fails the others stay on.

items.stem: Explain why adding another resistor in parallel decreases the total resistance of a circuit.
items.answer: It provides an extra path for charge, so more current flows for the same p.d.; R = V/I is smaller.

items.stem: Resistors of 12 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel across a 9 V supply. Calculate (a) the current in each resistor, (b) the total current and (c) the combined resistance.
items.markingKey: (a) I = V/R in each branch (full 9 V across each) [2]; (b) sum = 2.25 A [1]; (c) R = V/I = 9/2.25 = 4.00 Ω or 1/R = 1/12 + 1/6 [2].

items.stem: Resistors of 4 Ω and 4 Ω are connected in parallel across a 12 V supply. Calculate (a) the current in each resistor, (b) the total current and (c) the combined resistance.
items.markingKey: (a) I = V/R in each branch (full 12 V across each) [2]; (b) sum = 6.00 A [1]; (c) R = V/I = 12/6.00 = 2.00 Ω or 1/R = 1/4 + 1/4 [2].

items.stem: Resistors of 6 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in parallel across a 9 V supply. Calculate (a) the current in each resistor, (b) the total current and (c) the combined resistance.
items.markingKey: (a) I = V/R in each branch (full 9 V across each) [2]; (b) sum = 2.25 A [1]; (c) R = V/I = 9/2.25 = 4.00 Ω or 1/R = 1/6 + 1/12 [2].

items.stem: In a circuit, resistor P (3 Ω) is in series with two resistors Q (6 Ω) and R (6 Ω) that are connected in parallel with each other. The supply is 6 V. (a) Calculate the combined resistance of the parallel pair. (b) The 6 Ω resistor is removed. State and explain what happens to the battery current.
items.answer: (a) 3.00 Ω (b) It decreases: total resistance increases (only one path through the parallel section).

items.stem: In a circuit, resistor P (4 Ω) is in series with two resistors Q (6 Ω) and R (3 Ω) that are connected in parallel with each other. The supply is 24 V. (a) Calculate the current from the battery. (b) Calculate the p.d. across the 4 Ω resistor. (c) The 3 Ω resistor is removed. State and explain what happens to the battery current.
items.answer: (a) 4.00 A (b) 16.0 V (c) It decreases: total resistance increases (only one path through the parallel section).

items.stem: Explain why the current from the cell increases when a second lamp is added in parallel.
items.answer: A new path is added, total resistance falls, so the total current rises (each branch takes its own current).

items.stem: Explain why the branch with the smaller resistance carries the larger current in a parallel circuit.
items.answer: Each branch has the same p.d.; I = V/R so smaller R gives larger I.

items.stem: Resistors of 4 Ω and 4 Ω are connected in parallel across a 24 V supply. Calculate (a) the current in each resistor, (b) the total current and (c) the combined resistance.
items.markingKey: (a) I = V/R in each branch (full 24 V across each) [2]; (b) sum = 12.0 A [1]; (c) R = V/I = 24/12.0 = 2.00 Ω or 1/R = 1/4 + 1/4 [2].

items.stem: Resistors of 6 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in parallel across a 6 V supply. Calculate (a) the current in each resistor, (b) the total current and (c) the combined resistance.
items.markingKey: (a) I = V/R in each branch (full 6 V across each) [2]; (b) sum = 1.50 A [1]; (c) R = V/I = 6/1.50 = 4.00 Ω or 1/R = 1/6 + 1/12 [2].

How does the resistance of a light-dependent resistor (LDR) change as light intensity increases?
In a potential divider made of a fixed resistor and an LDR, the output is taken across the LDR. Explain what happens to the output p.d. when it gets dark.
items.answer: In the dark the LDR resistance increases, so it takes a larger share of the supply p.d.; the output rises.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: R of LDR rises; 1 mark: larger share of p.d.

items.stem: Explain how a thermistor in a potential divider could switch on a fan when a room gets hot.
items.answer: As temperature rises the thermistor resistance falls; with the output across the fixed resistor, the p.d. across it rises and can switch on a transistor/relay that runs the fan.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for R falls, p.d. share changes, switching device.

items.stem: A potential divider has R₁ = 2 kΩ and R₂ = 1 kΩ in series across a 6 V supply. Calculate the output p.d. across R₂.
A potential divider has R₁ = 4 kΩ and R₂ = 2 kΩ in series across a 12 V supply. Calculate the output p.d. across R₂.

A street-light controller uses an LDR in series with a 10 kΩ resistor across a 12 V supply, with the output taken across the LDR. The LDR is 2 kΩ in daylight and 30 kΩ at night. (a) Calculate the output p.d. in daylight and at night. (b) The lamp switches on when the output exceeds 6 V. Explain whether the circuit works as intended.
items.answer: (a) Day: 2.00 V; night: 9.00 V. (b) Yes: 9.00 V > 6 V at night switches the lamp on; 2.00 V < 6 V in daylight keeps it off.
items.markingKey: (a) 2 marks each using V = 12 × R_LDR/(R_LDR + 10); (b) 1 mark comparison with 6 V, 1 mark conclusion.

items.stem: A light sensor circuit uses a potential divider. The input p.d. is reduced to a quarter. Predict, with a reason, how the output p.d. changes.
items.answer: The output p.d. becomes a quarter.
items.markingKey: Using V_out = V_in × R₂/(R₁ + R₂): output p.d. ∝ input p.d.; factor = 0.250 = 0.250. 1 mark relationship, 1 mark conclusion.

items.stem: A light sensor circuit uses a potential divider. The input p.d. is doubled. Predict, with a reason, how the output p.d. changes.
items.markingKey: Using V_out = V_in × R₂/(R₁ + R₂): output p.d. ∝ input p.d.; factor = 2.00 = 2.00. 1 mark relationship, 1 mark conclusion.

items.answer: (a) 2.25 A (b) It decreases: total resistance increases (only one path through the parallel section).

items.stem: Lina builds a circuit with a 24 V supply: a 4 Ω resistor, then a junction leading to 6 Ω and 3 Ω resistors in parallel. (a) Calculate the combined resistance of the parallel pair. (b) Calculate the current from the battery. (c) Calculate the power dissipated in the whole circuit.
In a three-pin plug, which wire is connected to the fuse?
items.markingKey: The fuse is in the live wire so it disconnects the high-voltage side when it melts.

items.stem: Explain why the fuse must be placed in the live wire rather than the neutral wire.
items.answer: If the fuse blows in the live wire, the appliance is disconnected from the high voltage; in the neutral it would stay live and dangerous.

items.stem: Explain how a fuse and an earth wire together protect a person when the live wire touches a metal case.
items.answer: The current flows through the low-resistance earth wire; this large current melts the fuse, cutting off the live supply, so the case does not stay live.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: path to earth; 1 mark: large current; 1 mark: fuse melts/disconnects.

items.stem: A 1000 W metal-cased microwave oven is connected to the 230 V mains with a three-pin plug. Calculate the normal working current.

A 1000 W metal-cased hair dryer is connected to the 230 V mains with a three-pin plug. (a) Explain why the cable to the appliance must not be too thin. (b) State one advantage of a residual current circuit breaker over a fuse.
items.answer: (a) A thin cable has more resistance and would overheat with this current, risking fire. (b) It acts faster and can be reset.

items.stem: A 2400 W metal-cased iron is connected to the 230 V mains with a three-pin plug. (a) Choose a fuse from 3 A, 5 A and 13 A and justify the choice. (b) Explain why the cable to the appliance must not be too thin.
items.answer: (a) 13 A (b) A thin cable has more resistance and would overheat with this current, risking fire.

items.stem: What is the purpose of the earth wire in a metal-cased appliance?
options: To make the appliance work faster
To carry the normal working current
To carry current safely to earth if the live wire touches the case
To reduce the voltage of the supply
items.answer: To carry current safely to earth if the live wire touches the case
items.markingKey: A low-resistance path to earth causes a large current that blows the fuse.

items.stem: State three hazards of mains electricity and how each is reduced.
items.answer: Damaged insulation (replace cables); overheating cables from too much current (correct fuse/ thicker cable); damp conditions (keep water away, use RCDs).
items.markingKey: 1 mark per hazard with matching precaution.

items.stem: Explain why touching a switch with wet hands is dangerous.
items.answer: Water conducts and lowers skin resistance, so a dangerous current can flow through the body.

items.stem: A 2800 W metal-cased iron is connected to the 230 V mains with a three-pin plug. State one advantage of a residual current circuit breaker over a fuse.
items.answer: It acts faster and can be reset.

items.stem: Explain why a diode is drawn with a direction in a circuit diagram.
items.answer: A diode allows current in one direction only (forward bias); the triangle shows the direction of conventional current.
